new_rigorous_results: One-anchor fan lemma: after deleting the anchor column, (|A|-2)(|B|-1) cross edges are pairwise C7-compatible even when the defective center has only one cross neighbor.
The exact one-defective-row/star-row family above the Mantel threshold forces n^2/4-O(n) colors and therefore explicitly contains the R002 star-swap family.
Under BCM Case-1 property L4(2), same-color edges have edge-distance at least 2; if delta>n/3, every color class of size at least 3 contains a pair at edge-distance exactly 2.
A no-length-3-path certificate forced by a distance-2 same-color pair has an exact two-branch neighborhood decomposition: a near-two-clique core or a near-complete-split core.
first_strict_breakpoint: In the split branch, internal edges may concentrate on a small set of vertices with low degree into the large independent side. Neither the common-kernel lemma nor the exact one-anchor fan currently converts this robust missing-cross-edge/internal-density tradeoff into n^2/8-o(n^2) colors.
next_lemma: Normalize the split branch by a maximum cut and prove that either a large cross-good internal edge kernel exists, an approximate one-anchor fan exists, or the internal density supported by cross-bad hubs itself yields the required color lower bound.
claim_guard: The lemmas and finite checks do not prove the full asymptotic statement of Erdős #809 or the missing robust split-branch color bound.
